INTEGRATED WATER-ENERGY RESOURCE MANAGEMENT FOR REMOTE WATER-SCARCE REGIONS OF KAZAKHSTAN THROUGH SOLAR HYBRID TECHNOLOGIES

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Askar Abdykadyrov, Amangeldy Bekbayev, Yerkin Khidolda, Yerlan Sarsenbayev, Durdona Mustafoeva, Sunggat Marxuly

ABSTRACT

This study examines technological approaches to energy resource management in solar-based autonomous hybrid systems designed for water- and energy-scarce remote regions of Kazakhstan. Such regions are characterized by limited access to centralized infrastructure and a high dependence on diesel generators, which leads to increased environmental risks, including indirect pressure on local water resources associated with fuel transportation, storage, and combustion. A hybrid system integrating solar energy, wind power, diesel generators, and battery storage was developed and optimized using HOMER software. The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid configuration reduces diesel fuel dependency by 30%-50% and lowers energy costs by 25%-35%. Annual CO2 emissions are decreased by 1000-1500 tons, indicating significant environmental benefits. Despite relatively high initial investments (200000-400000 USD), the system achieves a payback period of 5-7 years. The study highlights the importance of incorporating local climatic conditions, including solar radiation levels of 1300-1800 kWh/m2 and wind speeds of 4-6 m/s, to ensure reliable system performance and sustainable resource utilization. From the perspective of environmental and water resource management, reducing diesel consumption contributes to minimizing risks of soil and groundwater contamination in remote regions. The findings confirm that solar-based hybrid energy systems represent an effective and economically viable solution for sustainable energy resource management in decentralized areas of Kazakhstan. This work contributes an industrial-engineering-oriented resource management framework for solar-based hybrid systems specifically adapted to Kazakhstan’s remote water-and energy-scarce regions, combining local climatic constraints with techno-economic and environmental metrics to support deployment decisions.
